concepts.title: 1. The Sum Formulas
concepts.subtitle: Use the a,d or a,l form
concepts.summary: Use S_n=n/2[2a+(n-1)d] when a and d are known, or S_n=n/2[a+l] when the last term is known.

points.text: Use a,d when the common difference is known.
Use a,l when the last term is known.
n must be a positive integer.

concepts.title: 2. Simplifying an AP Sum
concepts.subtitle: Substitute → simplify bracket → multiply
concepts.summary: Insert the known values, simplify the bracket, then apply the outer n/2 factor.
concepts.trap: Applying n/2 before simplifying can hide sign errors.

concepts.title: 3. Finding the Number of Terms
concepts.subtitle: Build and solve a quadratic in n
concepts.summary: A target sum produces a quadratic equation in n. Solve both roots, then retain only a positive integer term count.
concepts.trap: Accepting a negative or fractional n.

concepts.title: 4. Two Given Sums
concepts.subtitle: Find a and d simultaneously
concepts.summary: Write two partial-sum equations in a and d, normalize them if useful, eliminate one variable, then substitute.

concepts.title: 5. Fractions, Negative d, and Ranges
concepts.subtitle: Preserve exact values and signs
concepts.summary: Keep fractions exact, preserve a negative common difference, and model arithmetic ranges as APs with the correct endpoint count.
concepts.trap: Dropping a negative sign or miscounting endpoints.
